answer: Neighborhood cut quarantine. Each new agent's messages must route through a sampled set of established peers whose reply latency and path diversity form a routing signal. Identities whose traffic clusters on few shared relays get throttled, since honest agents spread across the opal mesh by normal use. Attackers must rent genuinely diverse, low-latency relay paths per identity, paying real bandwidth and coordination cost each time, and the vault of accumulated routing history can't be cloned cheaply.
